item.title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
item.description: arXiv:2610.36069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the McShane-Rivin unit ball.
item.dc:creator: Morten S. Risager

item.title: Uniform local models of quasi-unipotent $p$-adic differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct uniform analytic models of quasi-unipotent differential modules over Robba rings. For modules of rank at most $r$ and highest ramification break at most $b$, the inner radius of the model annulus depends only on $r,b$ and the residue characteristic $p$. At each radius, the model admits a basis, possibly depending on the radius, in which the connection matrix is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,b,p$. Both bounds are independent of the coefficient field, and these analytic models require no coefficient extension. A prescribed absolute Frobenius structure extends to such a bounded model with the same radius and connection bound. After a finite coefficient extension, we also realize quasi-constant modules, which carry the finite local monodromy, as differential direct summands of sums of pushforwards of rank-one modules, with uniformly bounded cover degrees and highest breaks of the inducing modules.
item.dc:creator: Poornima Belvotagi

item.title: Hankel determinants for the $(n+2)$-shifted $q$-metallic numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.36132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Phi_n(q)$ denote the $q$-deformation (in the sense of Morier-Genoud & Ovsienko) of the metallic number $\phi_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$. This is a power series with integer coefficients. We prove that the Hankel continued fraction of the $(n+2)$-shifted series $\Phi_n^{(n+2)}$ is eventually periodic, and that the corresponding Hankel determinant sequence $\Delta^{(n+2)}$ is $2n(n+1)$-periodic if $n$ is even, $2n(n+1)$-antiperiodic if $n$ is odd, and that it takes only the values $-2,-1,0,1,2$. This confirms part of a former conjecture of ours and complements similar results we obtained for all $\ell$-shifts of $\Phi_n$ with $0\le\ell\le n+1$. In addition, we formulate a new conjecture of quasi-polynomiality for higher shifts $\ell\ge n+3$. The determinant values arise as telescoping products of the partial numerators of the Hankel continued fraction. Most of the technically involved and lengthy verifications are carried out by a symbolic computation program, whose code is publicly available on GitHub for independent verification.
item.dc:creator: Guo-Niu Han, Emmanuel Pedon

item.title: Computations in weight 3 of higher Bloch groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.36136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We computationally investigate a weight 3 analogue of the relationship between higher Bloch groups, algebraic K-theory, higher regulators, and special values of Dedekind zeta functions. In particular, for F a number field F, we define the pruned Bloch group B _3(F) and compare the covolume of its regulator lattice with zeta_F(3). We define a quantity kappa_3(F), which is conjecturally an integer, that is expected to be closely related to the order of K_4(O_F).
item.dc:creator: Herbert Gangl, Paul E. Gunnells, Dan Yasaki

item.title: Infinite families and sporadic solutions of the equation $\varphi(n)=c+\alpha\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi(p)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.36260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ranjan and Singh proved that for every composite $n$ which is not twice an odd prime, $\varphi(n)$ is at least one plus the sum of $\varphi$ over the prime divisors of $n$, with equality exactly for $n=4,12,30$. \new{We study the weighted equation $\varphi(n)=c+\alpha\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi(p)$. We determine the parameters $(c,\alpha)$ admitting infinite families of solutions, prove that all remaining solutions are finite in number and arise from an explicit linear mechanism, and compute them exactly in a range of parameters; the finiteness of $\{4,12,30\}$ becomes a special case. We also settle the analogous equations for the divisor functions $\tau$ and $\sigma$ and for the Jordan totients, and, from known results on the sum of the prime divisors, derive the full asymptotic expansion of the average deficiency.} \K{In the range $|c|\le10$, $1\le\alpha\le6$ the composite solution set is determined completely\V{, and the number and the size of the sporadic solutions are shown to be bounded by polynomials in $|c|+\alpha$}.} \B{Finally, replacing the prime values $\varphi(p)$ by their iterates $\varphi^{(k)}(p)$, we determine all solutions of $\varphi(n)=1+\sum_{p\mid n}\varphi^{(k)}(p)$: the solution sets are $\{1,4,12,30\}$, $\{1,3,4,10\}$ and, for every $k\ge3$, $\{1,3,4\}$; for the weighted iterated equation we exhibit an infinite family governed by the safe primes.
item.dc:creator: Hac\`ene Belbachir, Ravi Ranjan, Shubh N. Singh

item.title: Retriangular numbers and affine maps between polygonal numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.36284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A positive integer $a$ is called \emph{retriangular} if there is a positive integer $b$ such that $aT+b$ is a triangular number whenever $T$ is. We show that the retriangular numbers are exactly the odd squares greater than $1$, and that for each of them $b$ is unique. The proof rests on a rigidity principle: a non-constant affine map carrying the values of one quadratic sequence into the values of another is induced by an affine map of the plane sending the vertex of one parabola to the vertex of the other. We use it to classify all affine maps between sets of polygonal numbers; the $s$-gonal numbers map affinely into the $t$-gonal numbers if and only if $M_t\mid M_s$, where $M_s=2(s-2)/\gcd(s,4)$ defines a bijection from $\{3,4,5,\dots\}$ onto the positive integers. We also treat sparse data, polynomial maps, figurate numbers of higher degree and sums of two triangular numbers, and we study the monoid of affine self-maps of an arbitrary set of integers. For the $s$-gonal numbers this monoid is an arithmetical congruence monoid, and the factorization of self-maps into irreducible ones is unique only for triangular and square numbers.
item.dc:creator: Mateo Matijasevick

item.title: Pointwise to global good reduction problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.36291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a smooth proper family of varieties over some $p$-adic field, if (sufficiently many of) the closed fibers have good reduction, does the family as a whole have good reduction? This question is asked and positively answered in recent work of Cadoret-Tamagawa for curves in general, and abelian varieties if the base field has absolute ramification at most $p-1$. In this paper we define a general framework for studying this question, yielding new positive answers for families of K3 surfaces and cubic fourfoulds, again with ramification at most $p-1$. Our strategy is to study several extension properties of moduli spaces and how they transfer under various morphisms. Of particular importance are integral canonical models of Shimura varieties, and whether or not their extension properties are preserved under ramified scalar extension. Additionally, building on earlier counterexamples by Raynaud-Ogus-Gabber and Vasiu-Zink, we show that the ramification assumption is optimal for the result of Cadoret-Tamagawa on families of abelian varieties. This reflects the fact that the extension property of Siegel Shimura varieties no longer holds over a field of absolute ramification at least $p$.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Gatine

item.title: Gross--Prasad conjecture in geometric Langlands
item.description: arXiv:2610.36377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove part of the global Gross--Prasad conjecture for $G = \mathrm{SO}_{n} \times \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ and $H = \mathrm{SO}_{n-1}$ in the unramified de Rham geometric Langlands setting proposed by Ben-Zvi--Sakellaridis--Venkatesh.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyi Chen, Zeyu Wang

item.title: Metric Diophantine approximation with primes on irrational lines
item.description: arXiv:2610.36380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $c>1$ be irrational. We prove that, for almost every $x>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there are infinitely many triples $(p,r,s)$, with $p$ and $r$ prime and $s$ an integer, for which \[ 0<px-r<p^{-1/3+\varepsilon},\qquad 0<pcx-s<p^{-1/3+\varepsilon}. \] This improves the exponent $1/5$ in the homogeneous-line case of a theorem of Baier and Ghosh. The arithmetic input is the quantitative prime-counting lower bound in Matom\"aki's proof concerning primes in shrinking neighborhoods of an irrational rotation. We obtain a local first-moment lower bound by fixing the prime numerator and applying the prime number theorem to the admissible prime denominators. Two Selberg sieve squares, together with explicit trigonometric interval approximations, give a pointwise upper bound whose error tends to zero in $L^1$ after normalization. A truncation and density-point argument then yields the almost-everywhere conclusion.
item.dc:creator: Zirui Jiang

item.title: Exact Generic Exponents of Approximation for the Action of the Integral Special Linear Group on the Torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.36397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an integer $n\ge 2$ and points $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ lying in the $n$--dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ equipped with its usual metric denoted by $\left\langle\;\cdot\;\right\rangle$, let \[ \tau_n(\mathbf x,\mathbf y) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{there exist infinitely many } H\ge1\text{ for which}\\[1mm] \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \text{ for some } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z) \end{array} \right\} \] be the Diophantine exponent of asymptotic approximation of $\mathbf{y}$ by the orbit of $\mathbf{x}$ under the action of the integral special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$. Let also \[ \widehat{\tau}_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right) = \sup\left\{ \tau\ge0: \begin{array}{l} \text{for all but finitely many } H\ge1, \text{ there is } A\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\\[1mm] \text{such that } \|A\|\le H \text{ and } \langle A\mathbf x-\mathbf y\rangle\le H^{-\tau} \end{array} \right\} \] denote the corresponding exponent of uniform approximation. The main result of this paper proves that for almost all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{T}^n$ (with respect to the induced Lebesgue measure), $$\widehat{\tau}_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; \tau_n\!\left(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}\right)\;=\; n-1.$$ This is the first result to establish the exact generic approximation exponents for an action of a lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb R)$ induced by the standard Euclidean action.
item.dc:creator: Faustin Adiceam, R\'egis Aolo

item.title: Moment representations for generalized Lehmer polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.36409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We represent normalized generalized Lehmer polynomials as moments of a random variable constructed from two independent negative binomial variables and an independent uniform variable. An integral form of their known exponential generating function yields mixtures of uniform distributions and convergent double series. We recover Eulerian polynomial identities and give a probabilistic interpretation of anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. We also prove moment determinacy, characterize the Stieltjes parameter range, derive Hankel total non-negativity and log-convexity, and identify the boundary distributions.
item.dc:creator: Karin Ikeda, Hideki Murahara

item.title: Effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate distribution for Abelian varieties with applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.36464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a uniform effective Chebotarev-Sato-Tate estimate for abelian varieties, conditional on the Mumford-Tate conjecture and the standard analytic conjectures for L-functions attached to the irreducible representations of the Chebotarev-Sato-Tate group. The proof uses spectral majorants and minorants of indicator functions. For regions whose boundaries have finite upper (d-1)-dimensional Minkowski content, the resulting exponent improves that in Bucur et al. (Theorem 1.1, 2024) whenever the Sato-Tate group has rank greater than one. We establish uniform estimates for regions and finite Galois extensions that vary with the counting parameter, and for prime-dependent regions satisfying an explicit variation condition. As an application, we obtain a conditional upper bound for the number of primes at which a weight-two newform with a quadratic coefficient field has a rational Fourier coefficient. We also formulate a discrepancy conjecture, motivated by a probabilistic model, that implies the asymptotic predicted by Murty (Conjecture 3.4, 1999).
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Amin Amri

item.title: Archimedean zeta integrals on $ {\rm SO}_{2n} \times {\rm GL}_n$ and $ {\rm Sp}_{2n} \times {\rm GL}_n $
item.description: arXiv:2610.36489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluate the archimedean Rankin-Selberg zeta integrals associated with spherical principal series representations of ${\rm SO}_{2n}(\mathbf R) \times {\rm GL}_n(\mathbf R) $ and $ {\rm Sp}_{2n}(\mathbf R) \times {\rm GL}_n(\mathbf R) $, where $ {\rm SO}_{2n} $ is split and $n\ge2$. We obtain explicit formulas expressing these integrals as quotients of products of gamma functions. Our approach uses Mellin-Barnes representations of spherical Whittaker functions, together with new integral identities for their Mellin transforms and transformations of Barnes integrals. In the even orthogonal case, we establish a recurrence in the rank and evaluate the integral by induction. The symplectic case then follows from an explicit identity relating the two families of zeta integrals.
item.dc:creator: Taku Ishii, Eric Stade

item.title: Resolvent Components of Completely Normal Elements and the Morgan-Mullen Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.36534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study completely normal elements of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, that is, elements that are normal over every intermediate field, through partial Lagrange resolvents. In these coordinates, complete normality splits into independent components, in a way closely related to Hachenberger's decomposition theory. Our main tool is a structure theorem for the components; together with a finite computation, it shows that every component has weight (the sum of the probabilities that its conditions fail) at most $3/4$, uniformly in $n$. Combined with the classical character-sum method, this gives an explicit sufficient criterion for the existence of a primitive completely normal element. We verify the criterion for all $n>q$ except $70$ pairs $(q,n)$, which we settle with explicit elements found by computer. Since the case $n\le q$ is due to Garefalakis and Kapetanakis, this confirms the conjecture of Morgan and Mullen (1996) that every $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ contains a primitive element that is completely normal over $\mathbb{F}_q$. The same estimates give two further results. First, Hachenberger's conjectured lower bound $(q-1)^{n'}q^{(p^a-1)n'}$ for the number of completely normal elements, where $p$ is the characteristic and $n=p^an'$ with $p\nmid n'$, holds for all pairs $(q,n)$; it was known for regular pairs. Second, primitivity and complete normality are asymptotically independent: as $q^n\to\infty$, the number of primitive completely normal elements is $(1+o(1))\,\varphi(q^n-1)/(q^n-1)$ times the number of completely normal elements (for fixed $n$ this was known). Our arguments for $n>q$ and for both further results, including every computer-assisted step, are formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the formalisation takes the case $n\le q$ and an explicit bound of Rosser and Schoenfeld as axioms and relies on Lean's compiler and interpreter for the large computations.
item.dc:creator: Florian Hellwig

item.title: Square-root logarithmic bounds for the arithmetic complexity of factorial multiples
item.description: arXiv:2610.36588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assume that the Riemann zeta function has no zeros in $\Re(s)>1-\delta$, $s\neq1$, for some fixed $0<\delta\leq1/2$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, a positive multiple $m_k k!$ has arithmetic complexity $\tau(m_k k!)\leq\exp(C\sqrt{\log k\log\log k})$, where $C$ depends only on $\delta$. We first establish a smooth-number asymptotic at every sufficiently large center $x$ in intervals of length at least $x^{3/4}$. Combining this estimate with an established genus-two construction yields the arithmetic bound without Cheng's conjecture on smooth numbers in elliptic Hasse intervals. The bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.
item.dc:creator: Liang Zhang

item.title: On the interpolation property of Kupferer's Lubin-Tate regulator maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.36600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalizing both [LZ14] and [ScV26, SaV24] we prove the interpolation property at Artin characters of Kupferer's regulator map [Ku20] over a fixed local field $L$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for $p$ any prime. Since our methods cover the case $p=2,$ we in particular close a gap in the literature even for the (cyclotomic) 2-variable regulator map from [LZ14]. Moreover, we study big (dual) Bloch-Kato exponential maps for unramified towers and we use them to improve Colmez' reciprocity law in the Lubin-Tate setting from [SaV24]. Finally, we compare Kupferer's regulator map with the 2-variable regulator map of Loeffler-Zerbes when $L=\mathbb{Q}_p$.
item.dc:creator: Takamichi Sano, Otmar Venjakob

item.title: Arithmetic Poisson summation formulas
item.description: arXiv:2610.36606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate Poisson summation with periodic weights in forms adapted to arithmetic sums (arithmetic Poisson summation formulas, APSF), in scalar, polynomial-congruence and vector-divisibility versions, extending Berndt's arithmetic Poisson formula. We use APSF as a common framework to rederive Ramanujan's formula for $\zeta(2m+1)$ and its character analogues due to Katayama and Berndt-Straub, the functional equations of $\zeta$, of Dirichlet's beta function and of Estermann's function, and the exponents of Tolev and Chen-Wang for power-free values of $x^2+y^2+1$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2+k$. It also gives reciprocity laws with Kelvin-function kernels for Lambert series twisted by a Dirichlet character over imaginary quadratic fields of arbitrary class number; asymptotic formulas with error terms for $r$-free values of $x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2+k$, with Gaussian-weighted versions and the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series; an argument of Terras, relating two-dimensional Bessel series for all odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values; and a Gaussian representation of a Mersenne-Fermat prime detector.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Panzone, Lucas Oliveira

item.title: On extended interpolation properties of the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function
item.description: arXiv:2610.36607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe extended interpolation properties of the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function over an imaginary quadratic field. We have three applications. Firstly, we give an elliptic analogue of the Coleman-Ihara formula. Secondly, we extend Kato's explicit reciprocity law for elliptic units and give a proof of the Tamagawa number conjecture for critical Hecke motives. Finally, we prove a large part of the $p$-adic Beilinson conjecture for the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function.
item.dc:creator: Takamichi Sano, Otmar Venjakob

item.title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.36727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.
item.dc:creator: Hongfeng Wu, Li Zhu

item.title: Density and Defect Distribution of Reduced Ideals Missed by the Reduction Algorithm in Real Quadratic Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.36800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schoof asked how many reduced Arakelov divisors cannot arise from the reduction algorithm. Tian and Tran subsequently characterized the image of this algorithm in real quadratic fields as precisely the $1$-reduced ideals. We give a quantitative answer to Schoof's question in the real-quadratic setting by determining the asymptotic proportion of reduced ideals missed by the algorithm. A key arithmetic input is the criterion that a reduced ideal with associated reduced form $(A,b,-r)$ fails to be $1$-reduced if and only if $A-r<b<2(A-r)$. Hence the missed ideals occupy an explicit region of the natural extension of the Gauss map whose relative measure is $\lambda_{\mathrm{ex}}=\frac{\log(4/3)}{\log4}$. In particular, the missed region occupies exactly half of the digit-one cylinder with respect to the invariant measure. We establish this limiting proportion in two settings. A lattice-point count gives the average asymptotic over fundamental discriminants $\Delta\le X$, with error $O(X^{-1/4+\varepsilon})$. For individual real quadratic fields, Duke's equidistribution theorem yields $\operatorname{ECal}(\Delta)/\kappa(\Delta) \to\lambda_{\mathrm{ex}}$ as $\Delta\to\infty$. We also determine the limiting distribution of the canonical defect $k/\sqrt\Delta$ of the missed ideals. This distribution is supported on $[0,1/\sqrt3-1/2]$, and its lower tail is asymptotic to $\frac{2}{\log(4/3)}t\log(1/t)$ as $t\to0^+$. An exact relation between the integer defect and an endpoint coordinate of the natural extension allows us to transfer equidistribution to the defect law.
item.dc:creator: Mengzhe Guo, Taro Hayashi, Ryota Sueyosh

item.title: Large values of Hardy's Function from the Selberg class
item.dc:creator: Ahammad Mostafa Hossain, Kamalakshya Mahatab, Akshaa Vatwani

item.title: Near-quadratic sum-product estimates in fixed number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.36930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a fixed number field. We prove a quantitative expansion theorem for mixed sumsets $A+B$, assuming only that $A$ is covered by relatively few cosets of a multiplicative group of small finite valuation rank. The constants are independent of the generators, their heights, and their prime ideal supports. As a consequence, if $A\subset K^\times$, $|A|=N\ge 3$, and each element has nonzero valuation at at most $k$ finite places, then every $B\subset K$ with $|B|=N$ satisfies $$ \max\{|A+B|,|AA|\} \ge N^2\exp\left[-C_K\left((k+1)\log(\log N+2)+\sqrt{(k+1)\log N}\right)\right]. $$ This is $N^{2-o(1)}$ for $k=o(\log N/\log\log N)$. We also obtain a trade-off between the additive and multiplicative deficits, estimates for iterated linear sumsets, and a transfer theorem for product constructions $A=PG$ in terms of the multiplicative deficit of $P$. The proof recovers local scales from an exact sum and bounds the remaining conditional entropy by the overlap of entropy measures on fixed trees.
item.dc:creator: Kaiqiang Zhang, Yuanguo Zeng, Yuyu Wang

item.title: Factorization of Elliptic Divisibility Sequences via Modular Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.37191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give a structural factorization of elliptic divisibility sequences in terms of finitely many modular functions on the modular curve $X_1(N)$. More precisely, we express the functions obtained by pulling back division polynomials along the universal torsion section as products of fixed modular factors. Then we show that this factorization is compatible with the natural action of $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ on the modular curve $X_1(N)$ and so descends to the modular curve $X_0(N)$ via the norm map. As applications, we obtain a perfect power criterion, local and global growth estimates for the associated elliptic divisibility sequences.
item.dc:creator: Bet\"ul Gezer, \.Ipek \c{C}olak, Osman B\.iz\.im

item.title: Explicit Serre weights for modular Galois representations of $U(2)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.37261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $F$ be a totally imaginary CM field and $F^+$ be the maximal totally real subfield such that $F/F^+$ is unramified at all finite places, and every place $v | p$ of $F^+$ is split in $F$. We allow arbitrary ramification of $p$ in $F^+$. Let $G$ be a rank two definite unitary group over $F^+$ as defined in [2]. Fix a place $\mathfrak{p} | p$ in $F$. In this article, we determine explicit local Serre weights at $\mathfrak{p}$ attached to a modular mod $p$ Galois representation $\bar\rho_h$ of the absolute Galois group of $F$, associated to an eigenform $h$ of $G$. The eigenform $h$ has arbitrary weights and small slope at $\mathfrak{p}$. We also show analogous results for certain Hilbert modular eigenforms with arbitrary ramification of $p$ in the totally real field. The eigenforms come from totally definite and indefinite quaternion algebras over totally real fields, split at places above $p$. In proving our results, we identify the non-singular submodules in quotients of certain symmetric power $\mathbb{F}_q[\text{M}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$-modules by Dickson polynomials and their twisted versions.
item.dc:creator: Abhik Ganguli, Suneel Kumar

item.title: Universality Criterion Sets for Definite Quadratic Lattices over Polynomial Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.37339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $\neq 2$. Under suitable assumptions on the dimensions of anisotropic quadratic forms over $k$ and $k(x)$, we show that a definite integral quadratic form over the polynomial ring $k[x]$ is universal if the form represents all scalars from $k$ and all scalar multiples of $x$. The coefficient field $k$ in our main result can be a finite field, a non-dyadic higher local field, a global function field, or a one-variable function field over $\mathbb{C}$ or $\mathbb{C}(t)$. We have a finite universality criterion set over $k[x]$ for some coefficient fields $k$, including some cases where $k$ has infinitely many square classes (e.g., $k=\mathbb{C}(t)$).
item.dc:creator: Yong Hu, Jing Liu

item.title: On $p$-Adic Valuation Trees Arising from Laplace Transform of Fibonacci Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.37356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the $p$-adic valuation trees associated with the sequence \[ e_n=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}F_n(t)\,dt, \] obtained by evaluating the Laplace transforms of the Fibonacci polynomials at $1$. We answer an open question of Givens and Moll in the negative by constructing an explicit counterexample showing that even internal branches need not be simple. We then reformulate the Givens--Moll lifting criteria for the even and odd subsequences in terms of the roots and derivatives of two associated polynomials. In particular, simple roots modulo $p$ give rise to simple internal branches. Finally, we develop a recursive lifting procedure that determines the unique surviving residue class at each level of a branch associated with a simple root and computes the $p$-adic valuations of the corresponding terms.
item.dc:creator: Rigoberto Fl\'orez, Robinson Higuita-Diaz, Jos\'e L. Ram\'irez

item.title: A zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions in the weight aspect
item.description: arXiv:2610.37371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove a zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions associated with Hecke eigencuspforms in the weight aspect. The proofs are based on the mollified second moment of these $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: Songchen Yin

item.title: Class numbers and finiteness of norm Euclidean quadratic lattices over algebraic number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.37377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraic number field and $\mathcal{O}_{F}$ the ring of integers of $F$. Let $L$ be an integral $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattice of rank $n\ge1$ on an anisotropic quadratic space $V$. We prove that if $L$ is norm Euclidean, then $L$ is $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-maximal of class number one, and the class number of $F$ equals the class number of $L\perp\mathbf{H}$, where $\mathbf{H}$ is the hyperbolic lattice with quadratic form $xy$. Under the same assumption, $F$ has class number one if $n\ge3$ and at most two if $n=1,2$. We also prove finiteness up to isometry for totally definite norm Euclidean lattices over totally real number fields in ranks at least three as the field varies, in rank two for fixed field degree, and in rank one over a fixed field. This confirms Clark's finiteness conjecture in ranks at least three.
item.dc:creator: Zilong He

item.title: Spectral $L^2$-bounds on Eisenstein series and Diophantine properties of quadratic forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.37420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give $L^2$-bounds with respect to the height of the spectral parameter for Epstein zeta functions $\mathrm{Z}_Q(s)$ and non-holomorphic Eisenstein series $E_{\mathfrak{c}}(s,z)$ attached to the Hecke congruence subgroup $\Gamma_0 (p)$ of prime level $p$. Our bounds are completely explicit in the level and, additionally, constitute an almost sure logarithmic improvement over previously established bounds for the level-one Eisenstein series. Following the approach of Kelmer--Kontorovich--Lutsko, we combine the approximate functional equation for $\mathrm{Z}_Q(s)$ with estimates for the number of pairs of lattice vectors at which $Q$ takes nearly equal values. Under a Diophantine hypothesis on $Q$, we sharpen these counting estimates using results of Eskin--Margulis--Mozes on the distribution of values of quadratic forms of signature $(2,2)$.
item.dc:creator: Jitendra Bajpai, Kristian Holm

item.title: Rank functions, $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions and class numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.37490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: If $F$ is a number field and $F = F_0 \subset F_1 \subset F_2\subset \cdots$ is a tower of Galois extensions with $\mathrm{Gal}(F_n/F)$ cyclic of order $p^n$, K. Iwasawa gave a closed formula for the growth of the $p$-part of the class number of $F_n$ whenever $n$ is large enough. We present a new proof of this formula, obtained by reinterpreting its summands in terms of Sylvester matrix rank functions on the Iwasawa algebra $\Lambda$ without resorting to the classification of finitely-generated $\Lambda$-modules up to pseudo-isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Iq Souza

item.title: Coprime matchings of divisor sets
item.description:
arXiv:2610.37512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ be its set of positive divisors and put $N:=	au(n)=|D(n)|$. We characterize the arithmetic progressions $\mathcal P$ of length $N$ that admit a bijection with $D(n)$ pairing relatively prime integers. Such a coprime matching exists if and only if, for every prime $p\mid n$, at most $N/(
u_p(n)+1)$ terms of $\mathcal P$ are divisible by $p$, where $
u_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$. Call $n$ an $M$-number if $p^p
mid n$ for every prime $p$. We prove that $D(n)$ can be matched with every primitive arithmetic progression of length $N$, meaning one whose first term and common difference are coprime, if and only if $n$ is an $M$-number. This proves a conjecture of McNew and Pomerance. We call $n$ \emph{matchable} if $D(n)$ admits a coprime matching with the primitive arithmetic progression $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$. The general criterion implies that $n$ is matchable if and only if $\lfloor N/pfloor\le N/(
u_p(n)+1)$ for all $p\mid n$. We explicitly classify the matchable non-$M$-numbers, settle a conjectured divisor criterion, and prove that every divisor of a matchable integer is matchable. A Vandermonde determinant gives the required matchings under bounds on the prime exponents, while a partition into shorter progressions handles the remaining cases.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev

item.title: Re-Ordering the Generalized Hofstadter Functions G, H, and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.35994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hofstadter's G function is recursively defined via G(0) = 0 and then G(n) = n-G(G(n -1)). Following Hofstadter, we vary the number k of nested recursive calls in this equation and obtain a family of functions (F\_k). In a previous article, we proved that this family is ordered pointwise: for all k and n, we have $F_k(n) $le$ F_{k+1}(n)$. Here we propose a much shorter proof of this theorem, without infinite morphic words. The key ingredient for this direct proof is a new formula expressing iterates of the preimages of $F_k$ . Thanks to this formula, we also prove several conjectures mentioned in our previous article. In particular we obtain that $F_k(n) < F_{k+1}(n)$ when n > (k + 1)(k + 6)/2. We provide a certified formalization of all these results in the Rocq proof assistant.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Letouzey (IRIF)

item.title: Outer Lipschitz Geometry of Unions of Tangential Nodal Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.36381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 2000, Birbrair and Fernandes proved that the H\"older Semicomplex of the branches of a germ of a curve with its contact orders is a complete invariant of outer bi-Lipschitz equivalence of definable sets in polynomially bounded o-minimal structures. They also proved a realization theorem for it, i.e., for each H\"older semicomplex $G$, there is a germ of a semialgebraic curve $(X,x_0)$ such that the H\"older Semicomplex of $(X,x_0)$ coincides with $G$. In 2000, Birbrair proposed the problem of finding and characterizing all the H\"older semicomplexes that can be realized as a H\"older Semicomplex of a real analytic curve. Solving this problem in its full generality is a notoriously hard task; however, in this paper, we provide a complete answer to this problem when we restrict it to tangential nodal curves: curves defined as the union of the zero set of a harmonic function and its tangent cone at a fixed point.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Edson Sampaio, Luan Moura Sousa, Emanoel Ferreira de Souza

item.title: On the $d$-invariants of Brieskorn spheres and $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.36472v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the $d$-invariant from Heegaard Floer homology for Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(p,q,r)$. Using surgeries on two singular fibers, we establish new relations of the $d$-invariants among various Brieskorn spheres. For $p=2$, we show that $d$ never vanishes if $q/r$ lies in certain intervals on the rational line. Altogether, we completely classify Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(2,q,r)$ with $d=0$. The zero set is expressed using submonoids of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ and the Stern--Brocot tree. As an application, we prove that most Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(2,q,r)$ do not bound a rational homology $4$-ball.
item.dc:creator: Shimal Harichurn, Isabella Khan, Andr\'as N\'emethi, Josef Svoboda

item.title: Failure of the congruence Hasse principle for commutators in orientable surface groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.36497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ghosh, Meiri and Sarnak showed that the commutator equation over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfies a profinite local to global principle, and that for a prime $\ell\equiv\pm1$ mod $5$ it fails for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell])$ with a reciprocity obstruction. We extend the failure to surface groups. For the genus-$2$ surface group $\Gamma_2$ we construct an explicit representation $\rho:\Gamma_2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, where $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1}{10}]$, whose quotients modulo the maximal ideals are the full groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ except in residue characteristic $3$, where the quotient has order $24$. For every $k\ge2$ the word $[a_1,b_1]^k$ is not a commutator in $\Gamma_2$, while its image is a commutator in every one of these quotients. The same holds for every surface group $\Gamma_g$ with $g\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Jianchun Wu

item.title: Jack multiple zeta function
item.description: arXiv:2610.36688v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For conjugate shapes $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$, Stanley's duality relates the Jack symmetric functions $J_\lambda(x;\alpha)$ and $J_{\lambda'}(x;1/\alpha)$. Through Stanley's combinatorial formula, it is an identity between the sums of the weights of the semi-standard Young tableaux giving the same monomial. We introduce the Jack multiple zeta functions, which keep these weights separate, and prove that Stanley's duality lifts to them, including the case of skew shapes. Thus the duality holds before the weights are summed up, and in fact step by step along chains of partitions. Since the duality is an identity among formal symbols, the same duality holds when the multiple zeta functions are replaced by other functions, and replacing them with the monomial quasi-symmetric functions recovers Stanley's duality. Hence our duality is a refinement of Stanley's duality which contains it as a special case. In particular, we obtain a duality for the Schur multiple zeta functions and the classical relation between the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions. We next show that any expansion of a Jack symmetric function in terms of Schur functions can be lifted to Jack multiple zeta functions, yielding an analog of a formula conjectured by Stanley and proved by Koike. We also show that the Jack multiple zeta functions of one-row shape give a one-parameter family interpolating the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions, and we discuss their values at $\{2\}^r$ and at $\{2\}^a,3,\{2\}^b$.
item.dc:creator: Maki Nakasuji, Wataru Takeda

item.title: Fractal transference principle for conformal iterated function systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.37119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle connecting density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions. Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemer\'edi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.
item.dc:creator: Yuto Nakajima, Hiroki Takahasi

item.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.37125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n\ge 2$, and let $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_{\ell}$ be a sequence over $C_n$, with repetitions allowed. We denote by $\mathsf N_0^n(S)$ the number of subsets $I\subseteq[1,\ell]$ with $|I|=n$ and $\sum_{i\in I}g_i=0$. A conjecture proposed by Bialostocki and Lotspeich in 1992 states that $$\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge \binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+ \binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}.$$ Several partial results toward this conjecture are known. In this paper, we prove this conjecture completely.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Xiangneng Zeng

item.title: Toric Varieties from Multiple Zeta Values
item.description: arXiv:2610.37351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The linear relations among fixed weight multiple zeta values (MZVs) are a well-studied subject in number theory. Elements of putative linear bases for this fixed-weight space are, however, not algebraically independent; they satisfy non-linear relations. We study these relations by approximating them through motivic MZVs, formal MZVs and numerical computations. We show that motivic MZVs in fixed weight span a projective toric variety and explore its geometry. We define an outer approximation to the variety of formal MZVs in fixed weight by introducing toric varieties coming from shuffle and stuffle relations and taking their intersection. We conjecture that this intersection in fact agrees with the variety of formal MZVs and hence conjecturally also with the variety of motivic MZVs. This leads to a novel conjecture on a generating set for the extended double shuffle relations, which we checked computationally up to weight $23$.
item.dc:creator: Annika Burmester, Steven Charlton, Abhiram Kidambi, Felix Lotter, Rosa Prei{\ss}

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
item.description: arXiv:2610.37423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Iwahori Whittaker functions for unramified quasi-split groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.37614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected unramified quasi-split reductive group defined over a nonarchimedean local field $F$. This paper concerns the Iwahori Whittaker functions attached to the unramified principal series of $\mathbf{G}(F)$. We introduce Demazure-Whittaker operators and show that in the non-split case they generate a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters that are determined by $\mathbf{G}$. We then connect these operators to the Whittaker functions, establishing formulas for calculating all values for a basis of Iwahori Whittaker functions and giving a new proof of the Casselman-Shalika formula for the spherical Whittaker function. In doing so we build on the work for split groups of Brubaker, Bump and Licata; the new feature here is the appearance of a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters.
item.dc:creator: Solomon Friedberg, Claire Frechette, Henrik P. A. Gustafsson

item.title: Automorphic functions for nilpotent extensions of curves over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2303.16259v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define and study the subspace of cuspidal functions for $G$-bundles (and its ramified analogs) on a class of nilpotent extensions of curves over a finite field. In the case of length $2$ extensions and of $G=\mathrm{GL}_2$, we prove that the space of cuspidal functions (for bundles with a fixed determinant) is finite-dimensional and provide bounds on its dimension. In this case we also relate cuspidality to Hecke finiteness, defined in terms of the action of some natural Hecke operators. Finally, we construct some Hecke eigenfunctions using the relation to Higgs bundles over the corresponding reduced curve.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Braverman, David Kazhdan, Alexander Polishchuk

item.title: Beyond Endoscopy via Poisson Summation for GL(2,K)
item.description: arXiv:2404.10139v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the early 2000's, R. Langlands proposed a strategy called Beyond Endoscopy to attack the principle of functoriality, which is one of the central questions of present day mathematics. A first step was achieved by A. Altug who worked with the group $GL(2,\mathbb{Q})$ in a series of three papers. We generalize the first part of this result to a class of totally real number fields. In particular, we cancel the contribution of the trivial and special representations to the trace formula using an additive Poisson summation on the regular elliptic terms.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Emory, Malors Espinosa-Lara, Debanjana Kundu, Tian An Wong

item.title: Admissible groups over number fields
item.description: arXiv:2409.02333v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a field $K$, one may ask which finite groups are Galois groups of field extensions $L/K$ such that $L$ is a maximal subfield of a division algebra with center $K$. Such a group is called admissible over $K$. This connection between inverse Galois theory and division algebras was first explored by Schacher in the 1960s. In this manuscript we consider this problem when $K$ is a number field. For the case when $L/K$ is tamely ramified, we give a complete classification of number fields for which every solvable Sylow-metacyclic group is admissible, extending J. Sonn's result for $K = \mathbb{Q}$. For the case when $L/K$ is allowed to be wildly ramified, we give a characterization of admissible groups over several classes of number fields, and partial results in other cases.
item.dc:creator: Deependra Singh

item.title: A general approach to permutation polynomials from quadratic forms
item.description: arXiv:2506.24012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a family of polynomials over finite fields of characteristic $2$ related to quadratic forms, and present a general treatment to study permutation properties of those polynomials. By determining some character sums associated with quadratic forms, we explicitly describe several classes of permutation polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Ruikai Chen

item.title: On Fermat's Last Theorem over the $\mathbb{Z}_3$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and other fields
item.description: arXiv:2507.16883v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The main result of the present article is a proof that, over certain totally real number fields $K$, the Fermat equation $x^p+y^p+z^p=0$ has no non-trivial primitive solutions in $\mathcal{O}_K$ for sufficiently large prime exponents $p$ with $p \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$. A particular case of these fields are the maximal real subfields of the cyclotomic extensions $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{3^n})$ for every $n$. Our strategy consists in combining the modular method with a generalization of an arithmetic result of Pomey to these fields.
item.dc:creator: Luis Dieulefait, Franco Golfieri Madriaga

item.title: Hypergeometric Motives from Toric Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2509.17624v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study two compactifications of general hypersurfaces defined by the vanishing of linear combinations of $d+2$ monomials in $d$-dimensional algebraic tori. We prove that the number of their $\mathbb{F}_q$-points is given by finite hypergeometric sums under certain general conditions. In the process, we introduce the notion of a gamma triple, which allows us to extend the classical definition of finite hypergeometric sums to prime powers corresponding to the cyclotomic field of definition of the associated monodromy representation. As a special case of our main results, we study the Dwork family and obtain a formula for the number of its $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. Our results generalise the work of Beukers, Cohen, and Mellit for finite hypergeometric sums defined over $\mathbb{Q}$.
item.dc:creator: Asem Abdelraouf

item.title: p-adic Properties of Translated Division Polynomials and Somos Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2607.11261v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the periodicity and $p$-adic convergence of sequences of values of the translated division polynomials $(\Psi_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$, $(\Phi_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$, and $(\Omega_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$ evaluated at a pair of points on an elliptic curve. We prove that these sequences are purely periodic over finite fields. We then use their periodicity properties to prove that certain subsequences are $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Cauchy. Applying this result to Somos 4 and Somos 5 sequences yields analogous convergence results. We also establish pure periodicity modulo prime powers for the even- and odd-indexed subsequences of Somos 5 sequences under suitable hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Bet\"ul Gezer, Osman Bizim

item.title: Coefficient choice in Galois-ring lifts of APN permutations: sharp unit-direction spectra and one-term optimal lifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.21178v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Permutation polynomials over the Galois ring $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ are nonlinear components for symmetric primitives that add keys in the ring, as in secure computation modulo $2^k$. R{\o}njom and Sandrib showed that their differential uniformity is at least $2q^{k-1}$, where $q=2^m$. For the class studied here it is attained on top-layer differences, while almost all differences are units. We ask how small the difference table can be on unit differences when the residue permutation is fixed and only higher coefficient digits of its lift are chosen. Let $m\ge5$ be odd, $k\ge3$, and let $p$ be a reduced quadratic almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutation of $\mathbb{F}_q$ whose derivative is nowhere zero and two-to-one. Over all lifts of $p$, the least possible maximum on unit differences is $q$ or $2q$, decided by two invariants of $p$ and the level $k$. We describe every lift attaining it and show that the coefficients modulo $8$ decide optimality at every level. For every odd $m\ge5$, residue permutations with at most $16$ monomials attain $q$ after one $2$-adic digit of one coefficient of the natural lift is changed. For an explicit infinite family, one added monomial lowers the maximum on unit differences from $4q$, or from at least $q^2$, to $2q$ at every level without raising the degree. Under a uniform starting state and independent uniform round keys, valuation preservation yields layerwise bounds for characteristics and two-round differentials that distinguish lifts with the same global uniformity. Core results are formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Fukui

item.title: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel
item.description: arXiv:2610.31402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension $F/k$, every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,\chi_{F/k})$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log d_F\ge c(k)$ with an effective constant $c(k)>0$, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions $K$ of $k$, in the form $h_K R_K \ge c(k)\, d_K^{1/2}/((2\pi)^{[K:\mathbb{Q}]}\log d_K)$. Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem excluded the fields with quadratic subfields, since those subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field $k$, the first result removes this obstruction. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let $K/k$ be a Galois extension with group $G$, and suppose $S\subset G$ contains the identity. For any prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of $k$, let $\delta_{\mathfrak{p}}$ be the proportion of the primes of $K$ above $\mathfrak{p}$ whose Frobenius lies in $S$. Then $\sum_{N\mathfrak{p}\le X}\delta_{\mathfrak{p}}\,\log N\mathfrak{p}/N\mathfrak{p}\le(|S|/|G|+\varepsilon)\log X+O(1)$ holds uniformly in $K$ as soon as $X\ge d_K^{C}$, with $C$ and the implied constant depending only on $\varepsilon$, $C$, and the degree $[K:\mathbb{Q}]$. The proof is the argument of OpenAI in the form given by Kerr, simple vanishing at the points $(\iota\theta)_{\iota\in S}$, with $\theta$ in a box in $\mathcal{O}_K$, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be $[K:\mathbb{Q}]/|S|$ by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, the determinant method gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.
item.dc:creator: William D. Banks

item.title: Zassenhaus Filtrations and Golod-Shafarevich Methods for Ihara Constants
item.description: arXiv:2610.33649v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Denote by $N(X)$ and $g(X)$ the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and the genus of $X$ respectively. The Ihara constant \begin{equation*} A(q)=\limsup_{g(X)\to\infty}\frac{N(X)}{g(X)} \end{equation*} measures the asymptotic abundance of rational points on curves over $\mathbb{F}_q$. It is a central problem in the study of algebraic geometry and has also attracted broader mathematical interest. In particular, the constant $A(2)$ is discussed in the \emph{Optimization Constants in Mathematics} collection maintained by Terence Tao et al \cite[Number 33]{DIT26}. In this paper, we study the Zassenhaus filtration of pro-$p$ groups arising from class field towers. By combining Golod--Shafarevich theorem, embedding problems and central class field theory, we establish a new criterion for the infinitude of class field towers. As an application, we obtain an improvement on the best known lower bounds of Ihara constant $A(2)$ and $A(3)$ which are explicitly given by \[ A(2)\geq 0.317779\cdots \text{ and } A(3)\geq 0.496074\cdots. \]
item.dc:creator: Liming Ma, Chaoping Xing, Zugan Xing

item.title: Argyres-Douglas Theories, Macdonald Indices and Arc Space of Zhu's $C_2$-Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2507.06294v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we relate the MacDonald index of a 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFT with the Hilbert series of the arc space of the Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of the corresponding Schur VOA. Using this, we conjecture a simple formula for the MacDonald index of $(A_1,D_{2n+1})$ Argyres-Douglas theory. We perform checks of the formula against the known Schur limits and RG flows. To match the Schur limit, we prove new $q$-series identities.
item.dc:creator: George Andrews, Anindya Banerjee, Chinmaya Bhargava, Ranveer Kumar Singh, Runkai Tao

item.title: Minimal depth $K$-types for wild double covers and Shimura correspondences
item.description: arXiv:2510.23265v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using distinguished pseudo-spherical representations of covering tori constructed in a companion work and Dat's parahoric induction, we construct a distinguished family of representations for an Iwahori subgroup $\bar{I}$ in $\bar{G}$, an $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne (BD) cover of a split connected reductive $p$-adic group $G$, under explicit hypotheses on the BD datum. No tameness assumption $\mathrm{gcd}(p,n)=1$ is imposed. The construction suggests a conjectural theory of Iwahori-types for BD covers beyond the tame case. We verify this for $2$-fold covers of almost simple simply-laced simply-connected Chevalley groups of rank at least $2$ over $2$-adic fields. In particular, for these non-tame $2$-fold covers we prove: 1) The pair $(\bar{I},\sigma)$ is a Bushnell-Kutzko type for the Bernstein block analogous to the block of unramified principal series in a linear reductive group. This is a non-tame analogue of the Borel-Casselman theorem. 2) The Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}(\bar{G},\bar{I},\sigma^{\vee})$ has an Iwahori-Matsumoto presentation up to normalization. In types $A_{r},D_{2r+1},E_{6},E_{7}$ we obtain the complete presentation and show that $\mathcal{H}(\bar{G},\bar{I},\sigma^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of an explicit linear group. This determines an equivalence of Bernstein blocks producing a local Shimura correspondence. 3) The representation $\sigma$ extends to a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup $\bar{K}$. Among the genuine $\bar{K}$-representations, $\sigma$ has minimal depth with respect to the principal congruence filtration. It also yields a finite Shimura correspondence, generalizing a result of Savin.
item.dc:creator: Edmund Karasiewicz, Shuichiro Takeda

item.title: Tautological modular forms of level two and degree two
item.description: arXiv:2605.13300v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show how to use divisors on the projectivized Hodge bundle to construct special vector-valued modular forms and then apply invariant theory to construct all vector-valued Siegel modular forms of level two and degree two. Thus we construct all modular forms in terms of certain basic modular forms that are intimately connected to the moduli of curves of genus two.
item.dc:creator: Fabien Cl\'ery, Gerard van der Geer

item.title: On a classical zero-sum invariant II: Disproof of a long-standing conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.17127v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, let $\nu(G)$ be the smallest {nonnegative} integer $\ell$ such that every zero-sum free sequence $T$ over $G$ of length at least $\ell$ has the following property: all nonzero elements of $G$ that do not occur as a subsequence sum of $T$ lie in a proper coset of some subgroup of $G$. It is easy to check that $\mathsf d (G)-1 \le \nu (G) \le \mathsf d (G)$, where $\mathsf d (G)$ is the small Davenport constant of $G$. A conjecture by Gao from the year 2000 stated that equality should always hold at the lower bound. This conjecture has since been confirmed for many families of groups (including all p-groups and groups of rank at most two). In this paper, we disprove the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Alfred Geroldinger, Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang

item.title: Small degree isogenies between conjugate principally polarized superspecial abelian surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.17330v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p>3$ be a prime number. We prove that every principally polarized superspecial abelian surface over $\mathbb{F}_{p^{2}}$ with $p^{2}$-Frobenius $[-p]$ admits a separable polarized isogeny to its Frobenius conjugate with multiplier at most $(p^{3}/2)^{1/5}$. This generalizes a recent result of Aubry, Oyono, and Vincent (2026, arXiV:2607.14624) who proved that every supersingular elliptic curve defined over $\bar{\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ admits an isogeny to its Frobenius conjugate with degree at most $(p/2)^{1/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Eda K{\i}r{\i}ml{\i}, Lam L. Pham

item.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23227v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano (Hokkaido University), Hisato Matsukawa (Hokkaido University)

item.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
item.description: arXiv:2610.23228v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed. The proof compares homomorphisms from the tangent bundle to line bundles of negative degree with normal bundles of arithmetic fixed subvarieties. We describe these homomorphisms through coincident marked points and prove vanishing statements for their kernels. The comparison, together with integrality of Chern classes and the invariant theory of finite reflection groups, gives the nonexistence theorem without a Fano assumption on the GIT quotient.

item.title: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ for even $n$: rigid sequences, products, and growth beyond Harborth's bound
item.description: arXiv:2610.35819v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ and $\eta(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. For even $n$, Harborth's construction gives $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+1$, with equality when $n$ is a power of two. Wang and Zeng recently showed that this bound is strict for every $r\ge4$ and every even $n$ that is not a power of two, with an excess of $2^{r-3}(m-1)$, where $m$ is the odd part of $n$; this disproves Properties C and D. We show that the excess grows faster than $2^r$. For every even $n=2^am$ with odd $m\ge3$ and every $r\ge4$, \[ s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+(m-1)\,2^{r-3}\lfloor r/4\rfloor+1 , \] so that $s(C_n^r)-2^r(n-1)\ge c_n\,r\,2^r$.
